object_types.name: Account
object_types.definition: The customer entity in the system; everything hangs off it. Identified by account number, six digits, sequential, never reused.

source_references.excerpt: An account. Every account has an account number. That's what everything hangs off.
Yes. Six digits, sequential, never reused.

object_types.name: AccountNumber
object_types.definition: Unique six-digit sequential identifier for an Account, never reused.

source_references.excerpt: Yes. Six digits, sequential, never reused.

object_types.name: Product
object_types.definition: One of the products the company sells, identified by a product code.

source_references.excerpt: Product code. We have three: CORE, ANALYTICS, and CONNECT.

object_types.name: ProductCode
object_types.definition: Code identifying a Product.

source_references.excerpt: Product code. We have three: CORE, ANALYTICS, and CONNECT.

object_types.name: PricePlan
object_types.definition: The billing artefact that determines what a customer pays and how often; generates the invoice line. Identified by a plan code.

source_references.excerpt: The price plan. It's got a plan code, it says what the customer pays and how often. CORE-MO-49, CORE-AN-490, that kind of thing.

object_types.name: PlanCode
object_types.definition: Code identifying a Price Plan, e.g. CORE-MO-49.

source_references.excerpt: CORE-MO-49, CORE-AN-490, that kind of thing.

object_types.name: FeatureBundle
object_types.definition: What the customer gets -- the feature bundle: seats, API access, SSO, etc. Identified by name.

source_references.excerpt: When I say plan I mean what the customer gets. Starter, Professional, Enterprise. It's the feature bundle
Name. Starter, Professional, Enterprise. There's no code, which annoys me.

object_types.name: FeatureBundleName
object_types.definition: Unique name identifying a Feature Bundle, e.g. Starter, Professional, Enterprise.

source_references.excerpt: Yes. There's exactly one Professional.

object_types.name: Subscription
object_types.definition: The agreement that an account pays a given amount on a given cycle for a given product. Identified by subscription ID.

source_references.excerpt: A subscription is the agreement that this account pays us this amount on this cycle for this thing. It's got a subscription ID.

object_types.name: SubscriptionId
object_types.definition: Unique generated identifier for a Subscription, prefixed with SUB.

source_references.excerpt: Unique. Generated, prefixed with SUB.

object_types.name: StartDate
object_types.definition: The date a subscription begins; mandatory.

source_references.excerpt: Start date is always there. You can't create a subscription without one, the form won't submit.

object_types.name: EndDate
object_types.definition: The date a subscription ends; optional, present for fixed-term subscriptions or after cancellation.

source_references.excerpt: An open-ended subscription has no end date... A fixed-term one has an end date agreed up front

object_types.name: BillingPeriod
object_types.definition: The billing cycle of a subscription: monthly or annual.

source_references.excerpt: Monthly or annual.

object_types.name: SubscriptionStatus
object_types.definition: The status of a subscription: trialing, active, past due, cancelled.

source_references.excerpt: Trialing, active, past due, cancelled.

object_types.name: PausedFlag
object_types.definition: A separate boolean flag indicating a subscription is paused; overlaps confusingly with status.

source_references.excerpt: Paused isn't a status, it's a flag... it's a separate boolean, which is exactly why it causes bugs.

object_types.name: PlanChange
object_types.definition: A record of a change of price plan on a subscription, with an effective date and requester. Identified by change ID.

source_references.excerpt: It's got a change ID.

object_types.name: ChangeId
object_types.definition: Unique identifier for a Plan Change.

source_references.excerpt: It's got a change ID.

object_types.name: EffectiveDate
object_types.definition: The date on which a plan change takes effect.

source_references.excerpt: we need to know who made it and when it takes effect, and those are different dates.

object_types.name: RequestedDate
object_types.definition: The date a plan change was requested/made.

source_references.excerpt: Someone can make a change on the third that takes effect on the first of next month.

object_types.name: Requester
object_types.definition: The person who requested a plan change.

source_references.excerpt: It records the subscription, the new price plan, the effective date, and who requested it.

object_types.name: MRR
object_types.definition: Monthly recurring revenue; derived from the price plan price normalised to a month, not stored.

source_references.excerpt: It's worked out. It's the plan price normalised to a month. An annual plan at 490 is an MRR of 40.83.

ambiguities.description: The term 'plan' is used for three distinct concepts: the billing PricePlan, the product FeatureBundle, and a sales-negotiated deal. The sales 'deal' concept was explicitly deferred and is not modeled here -- should it be captured as a separate entity type in a future session?

source_references.excerpt: We've got two things both called plan, and the sales team calls a third thing a plan, which is the deal they negotiated, which frequently matches neither.

ambiguities.description: Whether the 'one active subscription per account per product' constraint applies only to active subscriptions, or to all subscriptions regardless of status, is not fully clarified -- the uniqueness constraint as modeled (external uniqueness on Account+Product) may need to be scoped to status='active' rather than applying globally, since a cancelled subscription for the same account/product presumably can coexist historically.

source_references.excerpt: An account has one active subscription. That was true when we only sold one product... So it's one active subscription per account per product.
One active subscription per account per product, enforced at the database level.

ambiguities.description: The 'paused' flag overlaps confusingly with the four-value status (a subscription can be both 'active' and 'paused'), and it is unclear whether paused should exclude certain statuses or is fully independent. No constraint was given clarifying interaction between PausedFlag and SubscriptionStatus.

source_references.excerpt: Paused isn't a status, it's a flag... It behaves like a status but it isn't one, it's a separate boolean, which is exactly why it causes bugs. If you ask the system for active subscriptions you get paused ones too.

ambiguities.description: The commercial/business rule for mid-term cancellation of annual subscriptions (run to term vs. prorated refund vs. credit) is explicitly undecided and parked; only the current system behavior (end date set to paid-through date, no refund mechanism) is modeled. Manual credits issued outside the subscription system are not modeled as a fact type since they were described as ad hoc, outside-system actions.

source_references.excerpt: What happens commercially when an annual subscription is cancelled mid-term -- run to term, prorated refund, or credit -- is undecided.

ambiguities.description: It is unclear whether a Subscription's denormalized 'current PricePlan' role is truly mandatory from creation, or only becomes populated once a PlanChange occurs (a 'brand new subscription' initially has no changes -- does it still have an initial current price plan set at creation, distinct from the PlanChange history?).

source_references.excerpt: And a brand new subscription has none. Right, none until something changes.
No, Sam, it does have a current plan field. The changes are the history, but there's a denormalised current plan on the record.

ambiguities.description: Email is mentioned as belonging to a 'contact' (not the account), implying a Contact entity type related to Account, but no further detail is given about Contact's identification, cardinality, or relationship to Account. Not modeled due to insufficient detail.

source_references.excerpt: Company name absolutely not, we have four accounts called "Acme." Email is on the contact, not the account.

ambiguities.description: A fourth product is 'in discovery' but not yet defined -- the ProductCode value constraint (CORE, ANALYTICS, CONNECT) may need revision when it launches; flagged as a temporal/completeness concern rather than a current-state error.

source_references.excerpt: Fixed today. There's a fourth in discovery, but I'm not going to pretend I know what it is.

ambiguities.description: It is unclear whether the change history and the denormalized current plan field can be reconciled programmatically, or whether disagreement is only detected manually. 'If those two ever disagree, the change history wins and the current plan is the bug' suggests a business rule/constraint that current plan must always equal the plan derived from the most recent effective PlanChange, but this equality/derivation rule is not formalized as a constraint here since it wasn't stated as enforced, only aspirational.

source_references.excerpt: And if those two ever disagree, the change history wins and the current plan is the bug.
